pr_title: [Merged by Bors] - [assets] fix Assets being set as 'changed' each frame
pr_body:
## Objective
- Fixes: #2275 
- `Assets` were being flagged as 'changed' each frame regardless of if the assets were actually being updated. 

## Solution
- Only have `Assets` change detection be triggered when the collection is actually modified. 
- This includes utilizing `ResMut` further down the stack instead of a `&mut Assets` directly.

issue_context.title: `Res<Assets<T>>.is_changed()` is true every frame, even when not changed
issue_context.body:
## Bevy version
0.5

## Operating system & version

Windows 10

## What you did

checked if my assets changed

## What you expected to happen

for it to only be triggered once after the assets were changed.

## What actually happened

`Res<Assets<T>>.is_changed()` triggered every frame without even changing assets

review_comments:
I'm curious if people even think that this should possibly trigger change detection?
Users (AFAIK) don't have a way to access the underlying `event` of the `Assets` collection, and wouldn't be able to to look at the side effects of this. 
Though of course, it is possible the we could depend on this behavior internally....
granted this would require a way to mutably access the contained value of `ResMut` without triggering change detection (which is something I can create a PR for later if desired).
I'd prefer not to add this; interior mutability is enough of a confusing asetrix on our change detection already.
Hmm yeah I think this might be a case where we want to ignore change detection. I don't think we use _any_ resource change detection internally, so we should be fine.
I'll create a second PR (after this one) that introduces a way to do this and then applies it to this case.
It'll be done via the new "DetectsChage" trait :)
